consequence.statement: The upgrade notes list the metric under Changed Metrics: it is now exposed as envoy_cilium_npds_init_fetch_timeout instead of envoy_cilium_policymap_<node-ip>_<node-id>_init_fetch_timeout, so monitoring that queries the old name needs to be checked.
consequence.remediation: Update dashboards, alerts and recording rules to use envoy_cilium_npds_init_fetch_timeout.

original.statement: In Cilium 1.17.0 the Envoy metric `envoy_cilium_policymap_<node-ip>_<node-id>_init_fetch_timeout` is renamed to `envoy_cilium_npds_init_fetch_timeout`, so monitoring that queries the old name needs to be checked.

decision.reason: [ev-3c947c36df35] lists this metric under "Changed Metrics" as renamed to envoy_cilium_npds_init_fetch_timeout. [ev-77f05428497a] says the prefix of all Envoy NPDS metrics was renamed from envoy_cilium_policymap_<node-ip>_<node-id>_ to envoy_cilium_npds_. The metric is still exposed, just under a new name. The upgrade notes do not say that anything fails, is rejected or must be migrated, so behavior-change (review) is the right kind, with low severity and a remediation to update dashboards and alerts that use the old name. A failure kind would claim more mandatory work than the evidence supports.
